Feliciano Viera was a Uruguayan Colorado Party politician and close Batllista ally who held several legislative and cabinet roles before becoming president from 1915 to 1919. As a legislator, he helped secure approval of rural land-tax increases by negotiating protections for departmental revenues, and later served as Senate president and interior minister. His presidency saw Uruguay take a pro-Allied stance during World War I, including breaking diplomatic relations with Germany and expressing support for Belgium.

Our World was a pioneering live, multinational satellite broadcast on 25 June 1967, linking broadcasters in 14 countries and reaching an estimated 400–700 million viewers across 24 countries. Coordinated by the BBC and European Broadcasting Union, it took 10 months and thousands of people to produce, using four satellites and dozens of control rooms; strict rules required every segment to be live and excluded political figures. The program showcased scenes and achievements from around the world, including the Beatles’ first performance of “All You Need Is Love,” and became a landmark in television history.

Einstein used vivid thought experiments to explore physical theories, but these scenarios provide arguments rather than new empirical data; their value depends on the reasoning they illustrate. His youthful pursuit of a light beam and later reflection on electromagnetic induction helped shape his conviction that physical laws should treat inertial observers consistently, though historians debate the early episode’s context and significance. The magnet-and-conductor example in his 1905 paper highlighted that different theoretical descriptions produce the same observable results, contributing to his search for a universal principle that led to special relativity.

Norway’s special operations unit, FSK, was established in 1982 to counter terrorism and protect Norwegian interests, later joining with the Naval Special Operations Commando under a unified special operations command in 2014. It evolved from earlier Norwegian ranger and parachute units, became more publicly acknowledged over time, and has worked with allied forces in operations including Kosovo and Afghanistan, as well as supporting police counter-terrorism missions. Candidates face demanding physical and mental selection followed by a year of basic training, with operators receiving further specialist training and using purpose-built vehicles and equipment.

After the Korean War, South Korea and the U.S. military tolerated and regulated prostitution in military camptowns, despite its legal prohibition; women faced stigma, exploitation, and low status, while official policy conflicted with everyday practice. The industry expanded amid postwar poverty and was organized to serve U.S. troops, with government measures and rhetoric sometimes framing the women’s work as economically patriotic. Estimates of the number of women involved vary widely, but prostitution generally declined as U.S. troop levels fell, and camptown life also reflected racial segregation among soldiers.

Dale Abbey originated as a hermitage at Deepdale, though its detailed foundation story—recorded by 13th-century chronicler Thomas de Muskham—blends historical context with legend. After several unsuccessful efforts to establish a religious community, it became a Premonstratensian abbey in 1204, grew wealthy through land and church revenues, and later faced uneven discipline before its dissolution in 1538. The chronicle also describes local landowners’ attempts to establish the community, including Serlo de Grendon’s grant of Deepdale to Calke Priory’s Augustinian canons.

El Salvador’s electricity system relies heavily on thermal, hydroelectric and geothermal generation, with geothermal output the highest in Central America; policymakers have promoted renewable projects to diversify supply and reduce exposure to oil prices as demand grows. Electricity access and system performance have improved, though rural electrification remains lower and the grid faces reliability risks despite reserve capacity. The document also describes changing sector governance, including a 2025 law expanding government control over market approvals and pricing, alongside plans and incentives for renewable energy investment.

Inter is a major Ukrainian television channel founded in 1996, now owned by Dmytro Firtash’s Inter Media Group, with an international service called Inter Plus. Since Russia’s full-scale invasion began in 2022, Inter has joined the state-coordinated United News telethon, though the war and financial pressures have severely affected its staffing and operations. Over the years, the channel has faced criticism and protests over alleged political influence, censorship, and Russian content, alongside major changes in ownership and editorial policy.

The Grammy Award for Best Hawaiian Music Album was established in 2005 after advocates sought recognition for Hawaiian music, and it honored albums until the category was retired in 2011. Winners included artists and producers associated largely with slack-key guitar compilations; Daniel Ho led with five wins and seven nominations, while six of the seven winning albums were released by Daniel Ho Creations. From 2012, Hawaiian recordings became eligible for the Best Regional Roots Music Album category.

Norway’s special operations force, Forsvarets spesialkommando (FSK), was established in 1982 to address terrorist threats, particularly to offshore oil installations, and developed from earlier Army ranger and parachute units. It later became increasingly focused on international missions, working with allied forces in Kosovo and Afghanistan, while also supporting Norwegian counterterrorism responsibilities and police operations. FSK recruits undergo demanding selection and extensive training, and the unit operates alongside Norway’s Naval Special Operations Commando under the country’s special operations command structure.

Dale Abbey near Ilkeston began, according to its foundation legends, as a hermitage in the early 12th century before being formally established in 1204 as a Premonstratensian abbey. It accumulated property and parish churches across the East Midlands, but its discipline and reputation varied, and after paying a fine it survived until its dissolution in 1538. Its 13th-century chronicle by Thomas de Muskham blends legends of hermits and visions with a more plausible account of local landowners’ repeated efforts to establish a religious community at Deepdale.

George Awsumb was a Norwegian-American architect whose eclectic designs ranged from neoclassical and Gothic Revival to Prairie and International styles, with a focus on public buildings and churches. After studying architecture and traveling in Europe, he moved to Memphis in 1919, where he designed landmarks including the Municipal Auditorium, Idlewild Presbyterian Church, and several schools and commercial buildings. His sons joined his firm after World War II, extending the family’s architectural influence across Memphis and beyond.

Komi Can't Communicate is a manga by Tomohito Oda about Shoko Komi, a high school student with severe social anxiety, and classmate Hitohito Tadano, who helps her pursue her goal of making 100 friends. Serialized from 2016 to 2025 and collected in 37 volumes, the series inspired a live-action drama and two anime seasons, with the anime streamed worldwide on Netflix. The manga had over 16 million copies in circulation by January 2025 and won the 2022 Shogakukan Manga Award in the shōnen category.

Durgapur is a planned industrial city in West Bengal on the Damodar River, near the Raniganj coalfields, with major steel, manufacturing, and emerging IT sectors. Planned in 1955, it grew around public-sector projects such as the Durgapur Barrage and Steel Plant, supported by coal resources, transport links, and skilled workers. It is also a large, diverse urban centre with high literacy, Bengali as its most widely spoken language, and a municipal corporation organised into 43 wards.

Mexico recognizes nationality by birth or naturalization, drawing on both birthplace and ancestry, and distinguishes nationality from citizenship; its laws also address the rights and restrictions affecting people with dual nationality. Nationality rules have changed substantially over time, especially regarding women, whose nationality was historically tied to their husbands, and children’s ability to inherit nationality from Mexican mothers. The history also reflects discriminatory immigration and racial policies, while reforms in the 1930s began limiting the loss of women’s nationality through marriage.

Durgapur is a planned industrial city in West Bengal, situated on the Damodar River and historically known for steel production, train-wheel manufacturing, and its dry dock; it is also developing as an IT hub. Established in the 1950s, its economy grew around coal, transport, skilled labour, and major public-sector industries, though several factories have since closed or struggled. The city has a population of over half a million, is predominantly Hindu and Bengali-speaking, and experiences very hot summers, heavy monsoon rainfall, and cool, dry winters.

The Used’s second album, *In Love and Death*, was released in September 2004 and became their most commercially successful record, later earning platinum certification. Recorded amid tension within the band and the deaths of two of vocalist Bert McCracken’s friends—including his pregnant ex-girlfriend Kate—the album explores love, loss, regret and reflection through an eclectic blend of emo, punk rock and alternative rock. Promoted with singles including “Take It Away,” “All That I’ve Got” and “I Caught Fire,” it was later reissued with the charity cover “Under Pressure” as a bonus track.

Durgapur is a planned industrial city in West Bengal on the Damodar River, known for steel and train-wheel production, its dry dock, and a growing IT sector. Founded as an integrated industrial hub in the 1950s, it expanded around major public-sector enterprises and benefits from nearby coalfields, transport links, and skilled workers. The city has a population of about 581,000, high literacy, a predominantly Bengali-speaking and Hindu population, and hot, dry summers followed by a rainy monsoon.

Durgapur is a planned industrial city in West Bengal, on the Damodar River, known for steelmaking, train-wheel manufacturing, its dry dock, and a growing IT sector. Established as an industrial centre from the 1950s, it developed around major public-sector projects and benefits from nearby coalfields, strong transport links, and a skilled workforce. The city has a hot, rainy monsoon climate, a 2011 municipal population of about 581,000, and Bengali is its most widely spoken language.

The 1941 Pittsburgh Panthers finished 3–6 under Charley Bowser, scoring 82 points while allowing 171, despite guard Ralph Fife earning first-team All-America honors. A difficult schedule and limited returning experience contributed to losses, including a 6–0 home defeat to Purdue and a 40–0 rout by Michigan. The Panthers then traveled to face defending national champion Minnesota, whose unbeaten streak and star-studded roster made them heavy favorites.

Joseph Ganim is a Democratic politician who has served multiple terms as Bridgeport’s mayor, first from 1991 to 2003 and again after winning election in 2015. During his early tenure, he pursued public-safety and redevelopment initiatives, but was convicted in 2003 of federal corruption charges for taking kickbacks from city contractors and resigned. After serving seven years in prison and returning to work at his family’s law firm, he made a political comeback and was reelected in 2019 and 2024.

From 1945 onward, South Korean and U.S. authorities tolerated and regulated prostitution around U.S. military bases, despite its formal illegality, while women involved faced severe stigma and low social status. Poverty after the Korean War drove many Korean women into camptown sex work; from the 1990s, workers increasingly came from other Asian countries and parts of the former Soviet Union. The system was officially promoted as serving military needs and earning foreign currency, with government figures showing thousands of women servicing U.S. and UN troops, though estimates varied widely.

South Korea’s military camptown prostitution system developed after the U.S. occupation and continued after the Korean War, despite prostitution being illegal; authorities tolerated, regulated, and at times promoted it around U.S. bases. Women—initially mostly Korean and, from the 1990s, increasingly from other countries—were subjected to stigmatizing labels and low social status, while women’s-rights movements disagreed over how to understand their agency and exploitation. The system was tied to military policy and South Korea’s economy: government figures and estimates vary widely, but prostitution near U.S. bases was substantial, officially supported in some periods, and declined as U.S. troop numbers fell.

The document argues that no universal extremum principle governs far-from-equilibrium systems; any such principle depends on the system’s specific constraints and dynamics. It presents macroscopic uncertainty as the source of apparent fluctuations and dynamical structures, and frames entropy primarily as a measure of experimental reproducibility rather than “order.” It also reviews conditions and examples relevant to non-equilibrium thermodynamics, including local equilibrium, nonlinear dissipative structures, discontinuous fluid flows, and coupled thermal, electrical, and chemical effects.

The Grammy Award for Best Hawaiian Music Album was presented from 2005 to 2011 after advocacy secured recognition for Hawaiian music beyond the Best World Music category. Its eligibility rules favored traditional music by requiring Hawaiian language on most vocal tracks, while also allowing instrumental albums; awards went to performers and production teams, with slack-key guitar compilations winning frequently. Daniel Ho led the category with five wins, but the Recording Academy retired it in 2011, and Hawaiian recordings became eligible for Best Regional Roots Music Album from 2012.

In Love and Death, The Used’s second studio album, was released on September 28, 2004, and became their most commercially successful record, later earning platinum certification. Recorded amid tensions within the band and producer John Feldmann, it was shaped by the deaths of two of vocalist Bert McCracken’s friends, including his pregnant ex-girlfriend Kate, to whom he dedicated the album. Blending emo, punk rock, and alternative rock, its songs explore love, loss, regret, and reflection; singles such as “Take It Away,” “All That I’ve Got,” and “I Caught Fire” supported an extensive touring and promotional campaign.

The Used’s second album, *In Love and Death*, was released in September 2004 and became their most commercially successful record, later earning platinum certification. Recorded amid internal tensions and the deaths of two friends—including vocalist Bert McCracken’s pregnant ex-girlfriend Kate—the album explores loss, love, regret and personal reflection through an eclectic mix of emo, punk and alternative rock. Supported by singles, music videos and extensive touring, it was dedicated to Kate and was the band’s final studio album to feature drummer Branden Steineckert.

Şanlıurfa is a large, predominantly Kurdish province in southeastern Turkey with a hot, semi-arid climate, steppe vegetation, and varied geological formations. The state-sponsored GAP project expanded irrigation and hydroelectric infrastructure, helping make the province a major producer of cotton, pistachios, peppers, grains, and livestock, though intensive irrigation has increased soil salinity. Agriculture remains central to the economy, alongside growing food-processing, textile, trade, and transport sectors; the province also has high rural poverty and out-migration, and hosts Turkey’s largest Syrian refugee population, many of whom work in agriculture, construction, and trade.

Yatterman is a 1977–1979 Japanese anime series and the longest entry in Tatsunoko Productions’ Time Bokan franchise, later receiving a remake, a live-action film, and a 2015 spin-off. It follows Gan and Ai, masked heroes who search for fragments of the Skull Stone and oppose the Doronbo gang, aided by a team of animal-shaped robots. The episodic adventures parody real-world people and places, while the story’s comic action centers on the heroes’ mechas battling the gang’s elaborate machines.

Established as an industrial hub from the 1950s onward, it benefits from nearby coalfields, strong transport links, and major public-sector enterprises, though some industries have since closed or struggled. In 2011, its urban agglomeration had about 567,000 residents, with high literacy and a predominantly Bengali-speaking Hindu population.

The document argues that no universal extremum principle governs far-from-equilibrium systems; any such principle must depend on the system’s specific constraints, and proposed principles generally apply only under restricted conditions. It presents macroscopic descriptions as necessarily incomplete accounts of microscopic states, with the resulting fluctuations driving dynamical structures, while entropy is best understood as a measure of experimental reproducibility rather than “order.” It also surveys examples of coupled effects, dissipative structures, and discontinuous fluid flows, noting the limits of classical non-equilibrium thermodynamics and recounting historical proposals such as Helmholtz’s minimum-dissipation theorem.
